question: Why did the static magnetic field promote single-crystal formation at high humidity?
expect: premise false: no measurable field effect; single crystals become more frequent at RH 59% independent of the applied field (abstract; Discussion)
rendered:
The document does not state that the static magnetic field promoted single-crystal formation at high humidity. In fact, it states that "the applied magnetic field does not produce a measurable effect on deposition morphology" (page 6). 

However, it does explain that higher relative humidity reduces the evaporation rate, weakens capillary-driven outward transport, and promotes single-crystal formation (page 6).
